Leave the hotel by 3:35 for the faculty lot and north clinic entrance. That still gets you to lab access near 4:15 for the 4:30-6:15 setup window.
Will stopping at the hotel first make it too tight? I’ll have the rolling case with handling materials.

Hotel first is fine if you are in the rental by 1:55. If baggage or the rental line pushes you later than 2:10, skip groceries and go hotel-to-lab only. If it pushes past 2:35, go airport-to-lab with the rolling case, then check in after setup.
Give me Saturday and Sunday leave times from the hotel. I don’t want to be figuring out the construction walk while half awake.

Saturday: leave the hotel at 7:15. That allows for the faculty lot detour, the walk to the north clinic entrance, and a few minutes to unlock the room before participants arrive. Sunday: leave at 7:30 unless you add a morning stop; traffic should be lighter, but the construction routing is the same.
And Sunday pack-up? I want Monday to be just checkout and the airport.

Sunday after class: reload all teaching supplies into the rolling case, do one check of the locked cabinet, and take the case back to the car before dinner. At the hotel, pack everything except Monday clothes and toiletries. Monday can stay simple: checkout by 10:35, top off gas if needed, return the car by noon, and keep the 1:55 flight untouched.
Put groceries in only if Friday is on time. The room setup is still confirmed, right?

Yes: queen studio, coffee maker, mini-fridge, desk, fitness room, and indoor pool are reconfirmed. Still no hot tub. Pool maintenance only affects Saturday daytime; it is expected to reopen Saturday evening. I’ll mark groceries as Friday Plan A, and if timing slips, move it to Saturday after teaching instead of crowding Monday.

messages.content: Raleigh is wrapped enough. The San Antonio pediatric neurorehab conference schedule landed, and the hotel block deadline is this Friday. I have a Friday panel and a Saturday hands-on lab, so I need Thursday arrival. Can you compare the official block against that nearby suite hotel and look at Thursday out, Sunday home?

Yes. I’ll treat this as a conference logistics decision first, not just a cheapest-room search. I’m checking Thursday arrival before presenter check-in, Sunday returns that don’t wreck Monday, and the two hotel choices: connected official block versus the suite property with stronger recovery amenities.
Exactly. Keep it compact, but tell me the caveats before I get attached.

Hotel comparison: the official conference hotel is the practical winner. It is connected to the meeting space, rated 4.2, has standard queen rooms, in-room coffee, fitness room, and an outdoor pool. Caveats: mini-fridges are by request only, and there is no hot tub. The suite hotel is the comfort winner: 4.4 rating, queen studio, coffee maker, mini-fridge, fitness room, pool, and hot tub. Caveats: it is farther from the meeting rooms, needs rideshares or a longer walk with materials, and cancellation is tighter.
What are the rates and cancellation differences?

Official block: $219 per night before taxes, cancellable until 72 hours before arrival if booked inside the block. Suite hotel: $244 per night before taxes when I first checked, but it has a 7-day cancellation cutoff and the first night becomes nonrefundable inside that window. The suite also adds daily movement cost and time. The official block saves hassle; the suite solves the fridge and hot tub issue.
I don’t care enough about a hot tub to haul lab stuff back and forth. The mini-fridge is the sticking point. How weak is “by request”?

It means the request can be attached to the reservation, but the hotel will not guarantee the fridge until arrival. Arriving Thursday afternoon helps, because they can assign from available inventory earlier. Plain caveat: if the fridge is essential for the whole stay, the suite is safer. If it is mainly for drinks and snacks, the official hotel is still workable with the request, hotel market, and ice as backup.
Okay. Flights next. I need to be functional, and Sunday can be afternoon, but not the late-cheapest thing if it gets me home useless.

Best practical outbound: Thursday 9:10 a.m. from Tampa, one connection, arrives San Antonio 12:58 p.m., about $368 right now. It gives a real buffer for bags, hotel, and presenter check-in. Cheaper but tight: 11:20 a.m. departure arriving 2:44 p.m.; still inside a 2-6 check-in window, but not good if anything slips. Least practical: midafternoon departure arriving after 7:30 p.m.; too late for materials drop-off.
And Sunday?

Best recovery return: 1:35 p.m. departure from San Antonio, arrives Tampa around 7:05 p.m., about $392 round trip paired with the 9:10 outbound. Middle option: 3:05 p.m. departure, arrives 8:38 p.m., usually a bit higher. Cheapest: about 5:55 p.m. departure, Tampa close to 11:20 p.m.; it saves roughly $70 but makes Monday harder.
Will the 1:35 return be too early if the Saturday lab teardown is real teardown, not just “leave a box by the door”?

It should work if teardown is completed Saturday before the evening reception, as the schedule suggests. Sunday would be checkout and travel only: leave the hotel around 10:45, rideshare by 11:05, airport around 11:25. If they add a Sunday presenter obligation or make you store materials overnight, then the 3:05 return becomes safer.
Could I do official hotel and just manage food without the fridge if they can’t provide one?

Yes, but I’d be clear-eyed about it. Workable plan: attach the mini-fridge request, bring shelf-stable breakfast/snacks, and use the hotel market or ice bucket for drinks. I would not count on storing anything perishable unless the request is confirmed at check-in. That is the main comfort trade-off for choosing the connected hotel.
What about the room itself? Queen room and coffee in the room, not just lobby coffee?

Official block currently shows a standard queen room available, and the room description lists an in-room coffee maker. The mini-fridge is the only in-room uncertainty. Suite hotel confirms queen studio, coffee maker, and mini-fridge, but again, it loses on connected location and cancellation flexibility.
Don’t book yet. Give me the decision shortlist as practical, comfort, cheapest.

Practical: official block plus 9:10 outbound and 1:35 Sunday return. Best for presenter materials and Monday recovery; caveat is fridge request/no hot tub. Comfort: suite hotel plus the same flights. Best room setup and recovery amenities; caveats are daily movement and tighter cancellation. Cheapest: official block plus the later Sunday return or tighter Thursday arrival. I do not recommend it for this schedule because the savings are mostly paid back in stress or late recovery.

Send the conference office the questions: exact presenter check-in hours, Friday room access before the panel, Saturday lab teardown timing, and whether the block can flag the fridge request. No holds yet.

Sent. No holds and no bookings made. I asked them to confirm Thursday presenter check-in hours, Friday panel room access, Saturday lab teardown/storage rules, whether the official block can attach a mini-fridge request, and the final cancellation deadline. I’ll keep the practical stack marked as official block plus Thursday morning arrival and Sunday 1:35 p.m. return unless their answers change the risk.

If the room isn’t ready when I get there Thursday, does that mess up check-in?

No. If the guest room is not ready, use bell services for your suitcase and take the presenter materials directly to check-in. The connected hotel matters here: you can be at the meeting level quickly without a second rideshare.
Please make sure the hotel notes don’t imply a guaranteed fridge. I just want it requested clearly.

Done. The reservation note says: “Guest requests mini-fridge if available; prefers assignment with fridge due to conference schedule.” It is logged as a request, not a guarantee. Early check-in is also only a request.
